content: First, emotions are generally complex and emotional representation models are correspondingly contested. Despite this, some models proposed by psychologists have gained wide-spread usage that extends to text-emotion analysis. Robert Plutchik presented a model that arranged emotions from basic to complex in a circumplex as shown in Figure FIGREF15. The model categorizes emotions into 8 main subsets and with addition of intensity and interactions it will classify emotions into 24 classes BIBREF23. Other models have been developed to capture all emotions by defining a 3-dimensional model of pleasure, arousal, and dominance.
